note: Spec instance for scripts/realdata_gate_analysis.py --spec --paired. PLACEHOLDER: A, B, CA and CB are null and MUST be filled in (from the frozen event curation) before any cell is analysed; the loader refuses to run while any endpoint window still resolves through a null anchor. A = the first frame of the absence (the frame on which the surface is fully occluded), B = the first frame of the return (the frame on which it is first revealed again). CA/CB delimit the control window, which must contain no part of the event.

anchor_semantics.CA: first frame of the control window
anchor_semantics.CB: last frame of the control window
anchor_semantics.expressions: a window edge is an integer or '<anchor>+<n>' / '<anchor>-<n>', resolved once by the loader

arm_roles.G: gated on the oracle absence window (the intervention under test)
arm_roles.GEST: gated on the ESTIMATED absence window (non-oracle timing)
arm_roles.GMIS: gated on a deliberately shifted window (sham timing)
arm_roles.GWRONGMEM: gated on the correct window but the wrong membership (sham membership)
arm_roles.GONES: the U configuration re-run with the gate present but vacuous; measures the within-prefix replicate floor

endpoint_notes.P1: the ghost window, read on the per-frame core ROI: the absence interior, three frames in from A so the occlusion is complete and two frames short of B so the return itself is excluded
endpoint_notes.P2: the clean return on the bounding-box event, three frames after B so the reveal transient is excluded
endpoint_notes.S1: the curated return tail on the bounding-box event, secondary
endpoint_notes.H1: the pre-absence harm guard on the bounding-box event
endpoint_notes.C1: the control window on the bounding-box event; it must not overlap the event and is where a sham arm is required to show its damage
endpoint_notes.profile_requirement: only P1 is read from roi:core; every other region endpoint is read from the event named by 'event_name', so each cell's f_box_profile.json must be produced with BOTH --masks and --roi_dir

PAIRED_CLAIM_RULE: CLAIM_CONDITIONS_MET iff every G-U pair on P1 exceeds its within-prefix replicate floor (|U - GONES| for that prefix, or PAIRED_MIN_EFFECT_DB where no GONES cell exists) AND no GMIS-U or GWRONGMEM-U pair exceeds the same floor in the same direction; DESIGN_WITHOUT_POWER when fewer than PAIRED_MIN_PAIRS complete U/G pairs exist; NOT_MET otherwise.
PAIRED_VERDICT_STATUS: DESCRIPTIVE. The paired analysis reports per-pair differences, their median and range, sign consistency, the mean difference with a paired-t interval, and the replicate floor. It performs NO hypothesis test: there is no p-value, no TOST, and no equivalence claim, and an interval below six pairs is labelled descriptive rather than inferential.
PLACEBO: within-run diagnostic only; the balanced-split spread of the U cells is reported to show what the design's own noise looks like and is NOT an input to the paired verdict
MASK_POOLING_RULE: an event carrying kind='per_frame_mask' is pooled by MSE weighted by its pixels_per_frame; frames with an empty mask carry zero weight and are dropped, so the unweighted constant-pixel-count pooling used for the bounding-box endpoints is never applied to a per-frame-mask endpoint
PAIRED_SIZING_RULE: n2_pairs = ceil(K*(sd_paired/DELTA)^2 + Z_A^2/4) on the paired differences themselves (one sample, not two), at DELTA = 0.30 dB
roi_source: scripts/event_region_frame_profile.py --roi_dir <dir>, one subdirectory per region (core/, ring/, object/), masks named <frame:05d>.png, uint8 0/255 at the render raster; each becomes an event named roi:<name> with kind='per_frame_mask'
